abstract: Prefoldin is one of the chaperone complexes that participate in protein homeostasis. Although it was initially described as a co-translational cochaperon that captures newly synthesized polypeptides and facilitates their folding by transferring them to class II chaperonins, nuclear functions have also been reported, including its contribution to transcription elongation and chromatin dynamics from budding yeast to mammalian cells. In this work, we have performed a proteomic search for prefoldin interactors in chromatin. Among others, we detected its physical association to FACT, the main histone chaperon that operates during transcription elongation. Lack of prefoldin provokes phenotypes associated to FACT perturbation, like chromatin-integrity defects in transcribed gene bodies, and derepression of cryptic transcription. It also leads to the specific alteration of FACT transcriptional dynamics in prefoldin-regulated genes. Lack of prefoldin also provokes co-transcriptional defects in histone dynamics, particularly in the eviction of macroH2A1, being this non-canonical histone a prefoldin-interactor itself. Finally, we show that these physical and functional connections with FACT and macroH2A1 respond to a single molecular phenomenon, and propose a model in which prefoldin would play a bridging role, enabling FACT to drive co-transcriptional eviction of macroH2A1-containing nucleosomes.
